title: Shrink Pattern
content: ### **Objective** Shrink or stretch 3D Garment Pattern horizontally and vertically without changing it in the 2D Pattern window. The default value is 100 percent (%) which indicates the natural state of the Garment material, in other words there is no artificial shrinkage or stretchiness. Use the function to express shrinkage after textile treatments such as garment washing, or use it temporarily to draw the inner layer against the avatar when dressing multiple layers of Garments for easier Simulation. **Location** Click Pattern ▶ Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ **Simulation** **Shrinkage Weft** /**Warp** **Operation** 1. Select a Pattern to shrink with 2D toolbar's ![Edit Pattern.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53146812707353) **Edit Pattern** or ![Transform Pattern.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53146825571737) **Transform Pattern**. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Click Pattern ▶ Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ **Simulation****Shrinkage Weft** /**Warp** 3. Enter desired shrink values. → The Pattern in the 3D window is now being shrunk accordingly.
content_description: This web page provides a concise guide on how to adjust the horizontal and vertical dimensions of 3D garment patterns for shrinkage or stretch without altering their appearance in the 2D pattern window.

title: Pleats Fold
content: **List of Contents** Pleats Fold Using Pleats Fold Pleats Fold Options **Pleats Fold** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZYJlNzBP3BM \- Auto assign fold angles based on the direction of the pleats. \- Select the **Pleats Fold** tool from the 2D toolbar. **Using Pleats Fold** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gVDbq6f6VRI \- Select the **Pleats Fold** tool from the 2D toolbar and navigate to the 2D Window. \- Click on the pattern to designate the start point of the pleats direction. Then, drag the mouse towards the direction the pleats will be folded. \- Double click to complete the guide line. \- Make sure to encompass all internal lines that fold angles should be assigned to. \- The Pleats Fold Window will appear. **Pleats Fold Options** * **Pleats Type YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ybOSk9LBLRU ** \- Select the desired pleats type among following options: knife pleats, box pleats, and accordion pleats. * **Options YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ULrUF0DfnwY**** ** * **REVERSE DIRECTION -**Change the fold direction of the pleats * **FOLD ANGLE** \- Set fold angle range that will be applied to the pleats pattern. \- Choose among Preset or enter the desired value. * **NUMBER OF INTERNAL LINES PER PLEATS** \- Decide whether two or three internal lines will be included per pleats. \- If internal lines that are supposed to have 180° fold angles are not established within the pleats pattern, select two for NUMBER OF INTERNAL LINES PER PLEATS. \- After the adjusting the options, hit OK. \- The outside folds will be highlighted in red whereas the inside folds will be highlighted in green. \- The pleats pattern will be folded based on the settings when the Simulation is activated. title: Non-testable Fabrics for CLO Fabric Digitization Service
content: **Fabric Type** | **Physical Properties Testing** | **3D Image Scanning** | **Comments** ---|---|---|--- Short Fur | O | X | Short Fur can be expressed by setting the Fur option for the Material type of CLO Fabric. Long Fur | X | X | Long Fur can be expressed by setting the Fur option for the Material type of CLO Fabric. Feather Yarns | X | X | The decorations on the fabric make it difficult to measure stretch and bending accurately. Foil | O | X | Foil can be expressed by setting the Iridescene option for the material type of CLO Fabric. Wide Stripe Fabric (Made of different yarns) | X | X | The combination of the multiple properties makes it difficult to measure physical properties accurately in a single fabric. Dangling Embellishments | X | X | The decorations on the fabric make it difficult to measure stretch and bending accurately. Complicated Novelty Yarns | X | X | The decorations on the fabric make it difficult to measure stretch and bending accurately. Multi-layer Fabric | X | X | If the multiple fabric layers are only partially attached, it can affect the accuracy of physical property measurements. Set the material properties in Property Editor. 3. Select the Front, Back, or Side tab to set the material properties for each side of the fabric. **📝****Note:** In the Back or Side tab, turn off Use Same Material as Front to apply different materials, or enable Use Same Color as Front to match the back and side color with the front. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38107403704601)** ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55473976669081) After clicking the Back tab and turning off Use Same Material as Front, the Swap Front & Back button appears, allowing you to swap the front and back material properties. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55473976673049) #### #### **Material Type** 1. Set the appropriate [CLO Material Type](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115015998728-Material-Type). #### #### **Base Color** **Color** 1. Set the [color](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360047316974-Fabric-Color) of the fabric. **Base Color Map** 1. Click the **Open** button to apply the Base Color Map. **📝****Note:** Through the option of [User Setting](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115002563607-Set-Default-Files), you can convert the color profile of the image to sRGB when loading textures. 2. Set the Recolor option as needed. **• Desaturate** Desaturate the entire Base Color Map to remove color and convert it into grayscale or black and white. **• Color Switch** ![Youtube Icon \(1\).png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55527645292185) [Watch Video](https://youtu.be/8sfPSGnNpG4) Easily and quickly switch the color of solid fabric to a new one without losing the accuracy of the chosen color. ![Switch Color.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38116673801369) ******📝****Note:** It is recommended to use the [Texture Editor](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360053351314-Texture-Editor#Click4) if the Base Color Map contains multiple colors, as it may not be switched properly. Please note that this Switch option is not synced with the Switch option in the Texture Editor. #### **Normal Map** Express uneven texture more realistically. 1. When a texture is applied, Normal Map is generated by adjusting the Intensity. 2. Or click the **Open** button to manually apply Normal Map image. #### #### **Displacement Map** Express thickness or bumpiness of fabrics or textures. You can find more detailed information [here](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360025439933-Displacement-Map-ver5-1-0). #### #### **Opacity** **Opacity** 1. Adjust the Opacity value to apply transparency to the fabric overall. **Opacity Map** Adjust level of transparency using a grayscale image map. 1. Set the mode to determine whether the map's alpha value is encoded in the RGB channel or the alpha channel. 2. Click the **Open** button to apply Opacity Map. #### #### **Reflection** **Roughness** 1. Set whether to adjust the Roughness with the intensity value or apply it as a specific map. 2. Adjust the values to express fabric gloss. 3. Check the Invert option to make the shiny parts becomes dull and vice versa when using the map. **Reflection** 1. Adjust the intensity value to express fabric reflection. **Metalness** 1. Adjust the value to apply metallics to the fabric overall. 2. Or click the **Open** button to partially apply metallics using a grayscale image. * The white parts of the map appear metallic. **📝****Note:** • When working with **Metalness Map** , control **Roughness Intensity** and **Reflection Intensity** level that are suitable for the metallic texture. (e.g. Roughness Intensity 10, Reflection Intensity 90) • For the non-metallic areas (matte), assign the same metalness map to **Roughness Map,** and turn on **Invert**. #### Go back to the List of Contents

title: Slider/Puller/Stopper OBJ Registration
content: Create OBJ Register OBJ **** Register your own OBJ file as a Slider/Puller/Stopper. **** **Location** Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Zipper ▶ Register OBJ Property Editor ▶ Shape ▶ ![plus_button.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/25189692962201) #### **Create OBJ** Check the requirements below when making OBJs in other 3D programs. **※ Essential** * Set the name of the MESH to **Slider and Puller** when creating an OBJ with a slider and a puller. ![Slider_Puller_name.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/900006815406) * For each type, adjust the position to suit the meaning of the axis. (If the position of the axis is not correct, the OBJ may not be loaded in the correct position) **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Slider** | **X-Axis** | Position the shoulder of the slider where zipper teeth insert on the X-axis 0. **Y-Axis** | The direction the slider moves is the Y-axis, Position center of the slider where the center of the zipper teeth aligned at 0 of the Y-axis. **Z-Axis** | Position the Z-axis 0 where the side of the zipper teeth is located. ![Slider.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/900006815306) **Sto** pper | The stopper configured on both sides must be made to be the same scale as the two OBJ axes. **X-Axis** | Position the shoulder of the slider where zipper teeth insert on the X-axis 0. **Y-Axis** | **Top Stopper** Position the point where the most end (top) of the zipper blade is in contact with the Y-axis 0. **Bottom Stopper** When the slider is lowered all the way, the point where it touches the bottom of the slider is positioned on the Y-axis at 0. **Z-Axis** | Position the Z-axis 0 where the side of the zipper teeth is located. ![mceclip6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/900007735143) ![mceclip5.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/900007735083) ![mceclip3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/900006815506) **Puller** | Place the position where the slider is attached at the origin (0,0,0). _**✨Tip:**_ The puller position is adjustable within the CLO. ![Puller.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/900006815366) **Slider & Puller** | Create sliders & pullers are created based on the slider axis. ![Slider_Puller.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/900007734823) **** #### **Register OBJ** 1. Click the Materials ▶ Zipper ▶**Register OBJ** in the top menus. Or, click the ![plus_button.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/25189692962201) button next to the type you want to register in the[ Zipper Style properties](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/48635221523353-Zipper-Style#h_01JZHVYK1Y1BS75CXPGTWRT63G). 2. After setting the following options, click the**OK** button. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Basic** | **Type** | Select the type (Slider, Puller, Stopper, Slider & Puller) to register the OBJ. **Name** | Enter a file name. **Scale** | Adjust the size of the OBJ. **Axis Conversion** | Change each axis of the OBJ. **File** | **OBJ** | Slider / Puller | Load the OBJ file you want to register. Stopper (Top, Bottom-Open) | Load each Top and Botton-Open OBJ file. The first OBJ loaded is placed in the direction of the zipper created first. Slider & Puller | Load a combined zipper OBJ file. Select and assign the mesh item of Slider and Puller in the Select Mesh menu. Teeth | ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55639131982745) Load the OBJ file to register as the zipper teeth. The spacing between the teeth is set to 0 mm by default. Adjust the spacing while previewing the result in the preview window. **Preview** | Check the imported OBJ file in advance. **Puller Position** | For Slider or Slider & Puller type. Adjust the sliders on the X, Y, and Z axes to set where the puller is attached. → The object is saved in the path below: Assets ▶ Materials ▶ Hardware_and_Trims ▶ Zipper ▶ Each object's folder **✨Tip:****** Registered files are automatically saved as presets and can be easily selected in the[ Zipper Style properties](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/48635221523353-Zipper-Style#h_01JZHVYK1Y1BS75CXPGTWRT63G).
content_description: This web page provides detailed instructions for registering your custom OBJ files as sliders, pullers, or stoppers in CLO 3D, ensuring proper positioning and compatibility for zipper designs.

Follow the indicated path below: 2. Click the ![__.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360039757274) **Browse** button to add a displacement map and modify below settings as needed. ** Displacement Map ** | As displacement maps are grey-scaled, their height is determined by the level of darkness of the grey color. **📝****Note:** Increase the image resolution and apply the Gaussian Blur effect to express the texture smoothly. ![Displacement_Map_tip.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360042515013) ---|--- ** Amount ** | Adjust the maximum height of the displacement map. content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on using displacement maps to accurately express the thickness and texture of fabrics in the Render window.

title: How to Prevent CLO File Corruption
content: This article describes why CLO's project file .zprj and garment file .zpac are corrupted and how to prevent them. **Problem Situations** ![001_unzip_error.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/23206992583705) * When launching CLO, get an error saying failed to read the project file. * When opening a project file saved on computer, it says it is unreadable. * When trying to save the file it says it can't be saved. * Opening the file takes a long time and eventually fails. * * * **Causes and Solutions** **Case1** **Disk Full... Actually** ![01 - Disk Full.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/23723388965273) * If disk space is insufficient during the process of designing and saving garments in CLO software, file corruption may actually occur. So make sure you have enough free space on your PC's drive. * We recommend that you have at least 20GB of free space to install and run the CLO software. You can make free space by deleting or backing up unnecessary files. * **See also:[CLO System Requirements](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000307168)** **Case2** **Mechanical Malfunction and/or Connection Failure** ![02 - Mechanical Malfunction.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/23723394477849) * File corruption may occur due to physical failure, disk error, or poor connection. * You can check disk status through the built-in disk management app or disk management utility on Windows and macOS. * In case of physical failure, contact your company's IT support department or the place of purchase. **Case3** **No Permission to File Read and Write** ![03 - No Permission.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/23723388981913) * All computer operating systems, including Windows and macOS, have permission to read/write your files. If you do not have or only have partial permissions to read/write, CLO file corruption may occur. Following post explains how to gain read/write permissions for CLO files in Windows and macOS. **[Disk access rights required when CLO running](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/17074279996697)** * If you are a corporate customer, please contact your company's IT/Security department. **Case4** **Blocking File Read and Write, or Data Tampering by Security Apps** ![04 - Blocking file RW.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/23723388997401) * Certain security programs, such as antivirus and Internet communication monitoring tools, may restrict Internet access and file creation of software such as CLO. **In their detailed settings, change the CLO software's Internet access and file read/write settings to "Allow".** * In the case of enterprise companies, they often use stronger security solutions than those described above, and in some cases, the files themselves created by CLO are tampered with. For corporate users, please contact your IT/Security department. **Case5** **Two or More CLOs Running Simultaneously** ![05 - Two or more CLOs Running.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/23723389001497) * If you use two or more CLO software at the same time, there is a possibility that the internal data of the CLO project file may be lost or corrupted. * All you know that it's a good way to save file often. And **if you need to save the final result, save it with only one CLO running.** **Case6** **External Storage Connection Failure** ![06 - External Storage.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/23723394520729) * File corruption may occur while reading or writing CLO files on external storage such as USB stick or portable hard disk. Although these are convenient, in reality, physical detection failures and connection failures are relatively frequent. * When transferring files between external device and your PC, it often appears that the file-transfer has been complete, but in reality, the all data has not been completely transferred. To check whether the file was completely transferred, simply compare the file size. * **In summary, allow plenty of time when exchanging files with external storage devices.** **Case7** **Network Drive or Cloud Sync Failure** ![07 - Network Drives.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/23723389012249) * If you use a NAS and various Internet cloud sync services, CLO files may be corrupted during file transfer over the network. Additionally, cloud sync services may have problems that removing or damaging files on the local computer during the sync process. * If you use a cloud sync service, set it to sync only specific folders, excluding folders and directories referenced by the CLO software. **For example, disable syncing your Desktop and Documents folders.** * * * **Read More** **1** For example, the size of the zprj and zpac files, including the CLO basic t-shirt and basic avatar, is approximately 20MB. If your files are smaller than expected, it means the internal data may be corrupted. If your project file is less than 1MB in size, it cannot be recovered because all clothing data inside the file has been lost. **2** When recording animations of flashy, heavy garments, the project file size will be very large, and this animation recording data may be fragile in some user scenarios. If you are recording a long animation, dividing the entire scene into sections as shown below will help prevent file corruption. ![008_animation.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/23728221927449) **3** Do not save files inside the CLO.app package. All Mac applications, including CLO, have a folder structure as shown below. It looks like a single icon, but multiple files and folders are bundled together to form an app. You can view it by right-clicking and selecting Show Package Contents. When you reinstall CLO or perform a live update, all existing files here will be deleted and replaced with the latest files. So never save your work files here. ![macOS_app_structure.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/34786160865945) * * * **File Recovery** If you would like to recover your file, please send us your problem file as is via **[Contact Us](https://clo3d.com/en/support/contactus/technical)**. And if the size of the file you want to recover exceeds 50MB, please send it via cloud sharing like as Google Drive, WeTransfer, OneDrive, or iCloud.
content_description: This webpage provides insights into the common causes of corruption in CLO's project (.zprj) and garment (.zpac) files, along with preventative measures to ensure data integrity.

title: 2D Pattern - Exporting Patterns from Yuka(SuperALPHA: Plus Yuka Pattern CAD System)
content: **Objective** Export patterns as a DXF file from Yuka in order to use them in CLO. **※ Note:** **Things to Check Before Exporting Patterns** * Confirm that patterns are closed shapes and all segments are connected. * Patterns must be closed in order to virtualize them in the 3D environment. * Confirm that patterns are not intersecting each other. * If patterns' light blue bounding boxes are intersecting, the overlapped area will not be exported properly. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005715647/60.png) **Operation** **DXF-AAMA Export** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: File ▶ EXPORT ▶ **Set TIIP/AAMA** (exps) ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005715667/61.png) 2. In the Set DXF Export window’s Pattern Outer lines only check **Margins (Cutting Lines) only**. Set the CAD type as **Etc.** and press **OK**. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005715687/62.png) 3. Follow the indicated guideline below: File ▶ EXPORT ▶**Set TIIP/AAMA** (exp) ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005715707/63.png) 4. In the Export DXF window’s File Type check **AAMA**. After setting whether or not the pattern has any margins in Print Pattern Classification, click the **Entire Area** on the right. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005768228/64__1_.png) 5. Press **Reference** on the Designate Export window to set the path to export the DXF and click **OK**. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005715727/65.png) 6. If a warning window saying “There is a warning pattern” pops up, click **OK** first and then check the pattern’s status on the window that appears afterwards. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005768248/66.png) 7. If all the patterns appear as “OK” then proceed to click **OK** to finish. If there are any that appear as “NG” find them and fix the problem. Patterns may have problems when outer and sewing lines are swapped. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005768268/67.png)
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for exporting DXF files from Yuka, ensuring patterns are properly prepared for use in CLO.

title: Create POM
content: **List of Contents** Single Group **Objective** Create rulers to check measurements of particular parts of 2D Patterns/Internal Shapes/Graphics. YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BbRGWeNBoq8 **Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Pattern Measure ▶ **Point of Measure** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![pom.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360039947034) **Point of Measure** **Operation** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated above. ** ** 2. Left-click on a **pattern or internal line** to start creating a ruler. ** ** **Single ** **** 3\. Double click the endpoint or hit Enter to complete creating the ruler. → A single POM is created and added to Object Browser ▶ POM Tab. **Group ** **** 3\. Double click the endpoint or hit Enter to complete creating the ruler. → A group POM is created and added to Object Browser ▶ POM Tab as a single measurement. → The length of the line linking two Patterns (one that is not placed within Patterns) is not included in the measurement. **📝****Note****:** * Hold down the Shift key to display vertical, horizontal, and 45º guidelines based on the clicked point. * To cancel while creating POM, press down the backspace key, ESC or Ctrl+Z (Windows)/Cmd+Z (Mac) keys on the keyboard. * While creating POM, right-click to enter Distance Moved. * Check 3D Length in the Property Editor after creating POM. * Pattern Outlines and Internal Lines can be [traced as POM.](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000307728-Trace) * If there is grading information in the pattern that created the tape measure, the length is displayed by grading size in the POM tab. * When creating a POM, press the **P** key on the keyboard to switch between the mode for generating it along a segment line and the mode for generating it as a polygon.(ver 2024.1) Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for creating and managing rulers to accurately measure parts of 2D patterns and internal shapes in graphic design software.

title: Edit Curve Point
content: **List of Contents** **Add** **Edit** **Objective** Add and edit curve points on Pattern outlines and Internal Lines. ** ****Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Edit Curve Point** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001096327/________.png) **Edit Curve Point** ** ****Operation** **Add** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location 2. Click the desired position of a segment to add a curve point. Or, Right click on a segment to split the segment by a curve point (ver 7.1) **Split into Two Lines** | Adjust by entering the length of both lines which are divided by the right clicked point, or by entering the ratio. ---|--- **Split by Length** | Enter the number of segments the selected line should be divided into. You can change the direction in which a point is added to a start/opposite/center basis. **Uniform Split** | Enter the number of segments the line should be divided into. The line is equally divided accordingly. → A free curve point is created at the selected point. → When a free curve point is added to an AI Bezier curve, the curvarture is changed based on the free curve point. **Move** 1. Click and drag a curve point or press the arrow key on the keyboard to move. To enter Moved Distance, right click while click-and-dragging the Curve Point **Distance Moved** | Type in the how much a segment or a point is moved. ---|--- **X/ Y Axis** | Type in how much a point is moved on X/ Y-axis. This option does not appear for segments.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for adding and editing curve points on pattern outlines and internal lines within the 2D editing tools.

title: Schematic Render
content:
**** Render 3D Garments into technical drawings for tech packs. ![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/48712050581273) [Watch Video](https://youtu.be/L0JaKhZleyI) **** 1. Activate ![Render Schematic On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/48712072683289) **Schematic Render** within the 3D window. 2. Set the following options as needed. **Main Menu** | **Description** ---|--- **Line Thickness** | Show or hide the silhouette line (the outline of the area where the garment and the background meet and the line of the wrinkled area inside the garment), seam line, internal line and topstitch line and adjust the line thickness. **Topstitch** | Set specifications of Topstitches to achieve a certain visual appearance in the Schematic Render. [![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/48712050581273) Watch Video](https://youtu.be/Gv2Byz5WTFI?si=RIVTNhd20zmdARTu) 1. Click the topstitch in topstitch tab of the Object Browser. 2. In the Property Editor, activate the **Local Schematic Scale** option by clicking the checkbox. 3. Set the topstitch parameters that appear below.
**Length** : Adjusts the length of each thread. **Spacing** : Defines the spacing between each thread. **Offset** : Adjusts the distance of the stitch from the edge of the applied line. **Thickness** : Controls the visual thickness of the stitch thread. **Width** : Sets the width of the stitch (especially class 500 & 600 stitches). **Distance** : Defines the distance between each stitch line. **Line Color** | Adjust the color of the line. **Garment Color** | Adjust the color of the garment. **2D Measurements** | ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55443545898393) Display 2D pattern measurements in the 3D window. **Color Chip** | Adjust the color of the measurement lines and text. **Text Size (%)** | Adjust the percentage to control the scale of the measurement text and lines. **Brightness** | Adjust the brightness of the garment.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for rendering 3D garments into detailed technical drawings for tech packs, including step-by-step instructions and customizable options for schematic rendering.

title: Edit Topstitch
content: **List of Contents** Move Properties Edit the topstitches to adjust their length or change settings. #### **Move** 1. Click ![Edit Topstitch On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/45467813423257) **Edit Topstitch** tool in the 2D toolbar. 2. Click and drag a point or a whole segment of the Topstitch to be edited. → The Topstitch is moved to the position. #### **Properties** * **Topstitch Style** 1. Select the Topstitch Style to change the properties. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Information** | Enter the information of trim. **Type** | Set the Topstitch type to Texture or OBJ. **Offset** | Adjust the interval between Topstitches on Internal Lines or Pattern outlines. **Stitch Count** | Create various different types of Topstitches up to five at a time. **Use Same Specification/ Material** | This option to configure multiple topstitches' Specification and Materials. **Specification**** **| **Shape** | Set the shape of Topstitch. _**✨Tip:** _Click the Add OBJ Topstitch button on the right to add and use your OBJ as a Topstitch. **[![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/25701546478617)](https://youtu.be/r60uueH5eeE?si=_9no49K1GmzWTThI&t=3975)**[Watch Video](https://youtu.be/r60uueH5eeE?si=_9no49K1GmzWTThI&t=3975) Set the Lenth(SPI), Space, Thread Thickness of the Topstitch. SPI stands for Stitch Per Inch, meaning the number of stitches within an inch. For example, 'SPI-4' means there are four individual stitches within an inch. For standard garments, SPI-11 is often being used. **Material** | Partially set the [material](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360047317454-Set-Fabric-Textures) of Topstitch. **Configuration**** **| **Face** | Select the face of Topstitch. **Number of Lines** | Set how many lines of Topstitches there are for a single style. **Distance** | It is possible to adjust the distance between the lines. The unit of the length can be set in inch, millimeter(mm) or centimeter(cm). **3D** | The Topstitch is more realistic in the 3D window. **Polygon Optimization** | ![Update.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/45467927193625) When the Type is set to OBJ, the polygon count is optimized based on the value you enter to improve performance. ![20 Topstitch I Polygon Optimization.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/45467984687129) ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/45467813424921) * **T****opstitch** 1. Click on the Topstitch created in the pattern to change its properties individually. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Topstitch Property** | Change the style of the selected Topstitch. **Extend** | When the start or end point of a Topstitch does not reach or sticks out of the Pattern outline, extend it to fit to the Pattern. **Corner**** **| **Curved** | Set Topstitch corner type to extend the stitch more smoothly at corners. **Right Angled** | Set the Topstitch to be a right angle in the corner of the pattern. **Smooth ** | Set it to continue naturally if the edge of the Topstitch is broken. **Offset** | Set the Z Offset of the Topstitch. **Placement** | Use the Flip function to set a Topstitch on an Internal Shape/Line in a different direction (inside and outside). Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide for editing and customizing topstitches, including their properties, styles, and placement in garment design.

title: [Property] Flip Topstitch
content: ### Objective Use the Flip function to set a Topstitch on an Internal Shape/Line in a different direction (inside and outside). When setting the Topstitch on the Pattern's cutting line, the Topstitches always appear on the inside of a Garment and the Flip function gets deactivated. **Location** Property Editor ▶ Placement ▶**Flip** **Operation** 1. Select a Topstitch with ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005670908/_________.png) **Edit Topstitch** tool in the 2D window for changing its properties. → Topstitch properties appear on the Property Editor. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor ▶ Placement ▶**Flip** → The Topstitch direction is now being changed.

title: OBJ Trim

title: Troubleshooting AI Import Failures
content: **List of Contents** Case 1 (There are Pattern points that are too close together) Case 2 (Pattern outlines are intersecting) Case 3 (This is an unsupported file type.) **Objective** Learn how to fix AI import failures respective to the types of error messages. **Case 1** ![Case_1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115018795768/Case_1.png) **Cause of Error:** When the points on the patterns are too close to each other. **Solution A - Delete & Join Points in Adobe Illustrator** 1. Open the file with issue in the Adobe Illustrator. 2. Find points too closed to each other and delete one of them. → As the point is deleted, the line is disconnected. 3. Use the Average and Join function to reconnect the line. 4. Save the file again and open in CLO. → The pattern file opens properly in CLO. **Solution B - Adjust Pattern Size in CLO** 1. Navigate to the Main Menu and select File > Import > **Adobe (AI/PDF)**. → The Import AI/PDF window appears. 2. Deselect Auto Scale. 3. Increase the Scale percentage or select larger pattern unit and select OK. → The pattern file opens properly. **※ Note:** * If the pattern file still does not open properly, further increase the Scale percentage or select even larger pattern unit. Then, open the file again. * When the percentage and the unit is changed, the size of the pattern imported in CLO may differ from the original pattern size. **Case 2** ![Case_2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115018703567/Case_2.png) **Cause of Error:** When the lines on patterns are intersecting. **Solution** 1. Open the file with issue in Adobe Illustrator. 2. Find and edit the intersecting lines. 3. Save the file and re-open in CLO. → The file opens properly. **Case 3** ![Case_3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115018703587/Case_3.png) **Cause of Error A:** When the Create PDF Compatible File option is not checked when saving the file in Adobe Illustrator. **Solution** 1. Open the file with issue in Adobe Illustrator. 2. Navigate to the Main Menu > File > Save as... 3. Assign the saving path and the file name. Then, click Save. 4. Check Create PDF Compatible File and click OK. 5. Reopen the file in CLO. → The file opens properly. **Cause of Error B:** When a line of a pattern is disconnected. ** Solution ** 1. Open the file with issue in Adobe Illustrator. 2. Find the disconnected pattern outline. 3. Use the Average and Join function to reconnect the line. 4. Save the file again and open in CLO. → The pattern file opens properly in CLO. **※ Note: ** * For**Case 2** and **Case 3** , create a rectangle surrounding all patterns with issue, save in Adobe Illustrator, and then reopen in CLO as internal lines to open them without any pattern modification. * To use the Internal Lines as Patterns, use the [**Trace tool** ](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000307728) or the [**Clone as Pattern** ](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000343287)option to convert Internal Lines to Patterns. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides solutions for resolving common AI import failures in CLO, including issues with closely spaced pattern points, intersecting outlines, and unsupported file types.

content: Prepare PBR Images File Naming Rule Import PBR Images YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kOsqnvb583Q?si=I1qbBbJ8gFm1V7nJ Import other PBR maps once after importing a Base Color Map. #### **Prepare PBR Images** 1. Gather all PBR map images in the same folder on the PC. 2. Change images’ names according to the file naming rule. → Apply the rules for importing all PBR Maps. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44153023120153) ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44161076961305) #### **File Naming Rule** Follow the image naming rule with 3 components with the order 'Image Name_PBR Map Name' * **Image Name** It should be placed at the beginning. The name can be customized. Use the same image name to recognize that those map images are in the same group. * **Underscore _** It should be placed in the middle. * **PBR Map Name** It should be placed at the end. The name needs to follow the chart below. Affect the image import position in CLO Property Editor. **PBR Map** | **Name** | **Example** ---|---|--- **Base Color Map** | Image Name Image Name_BASE Image Name_basecolor Image Name_color Image Name_COL Image Name_diffuse Image Name_DIFF | ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44153023121305) **Normal Map** | Image Name_normal Image Name_NRM | ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44153012931993) **Displacement Map** | Image Name_displacement Image Name_DISP Image Name_height | ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44153012933657) **Opacity Map** | Image Name_opacity Image Name_OPA Image Name_alpha Image Name_ALP | ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44153023152665) **Roughness Map** | Image Name_roughness Image Name_ROUGH | ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44153023154201) **Metalness Map** | Image Name_metalness Image Name_MTL | ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44153012936985) **📝Note:** * Uppercase and lowercase letters are acceptable. * Image Name can be in English or Chinese wording. ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44161076961305) #### **Import PBR Images** 1. Import a Base Color Map in Property Editor; or add a new Base Color Map to replace the existing Base Color Map in Property Editor. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44153012939673) 2. Click **Yes** or **No** in the popup menu. → Click **Yes** to add Base Color Map and other PBR maps in Property Editor simultaneously. → Click **No** to add Base Color Map only. Other PBR maps in Property Editor won't be imported or updated. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44153012940697)

title: "MSVCP100.dll was not found" error - troubleshooting
content: This article is for Windows users only. When running the CLO software, it may not run with the following error. This is caused by missing or outdated Visual C++ Redistributable which essential Windows components to running CLO software. Additionally, the latest CLO installer includes the Visual C++ Redistributable package for that version, which is installed together with the CLO installation. ![dll2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001172007) **How to solve** * Visit [Microsoft website](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-US/cpp/windows/latest-supported-vc-redist?view=msvc-170), then download and install the latest Visual C++ Redistributable. * For Windows 10 or 11 computer users with an Intel or AMD processor, download the X64 architecture as shown below. ![002_x64.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/45219705062041) **Note** * In some cases, you may need to remove older versions of the Visual C++ Redistributable installed on your computer. * The Visual C++ Redistributable is backwards compatible with older versions, so we recommend installing only the most recent version.
content_description: This webpage provides essential troubleshooting guidance for Windows users encountering errors with CLO software due to missing or outdated Visual C++ Redistributable components.

This allows you to swap the face while keeping the background result. 2. Generate a face image to be composited by entering prompts or upload it directly. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Text Prompt** | Select gender, age, and ethnicity, and enter your prompt. **✨ Writing Tips:** * **List the words. ** Listing the desired words rather than long descriptive sentences can generate more effective results. * **Emphasize certain words more. ** If parentheses are used around a word you want to emphasize, it carries more weight.
